page: Amazon Web Services x1e.2xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the Xen hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon E7-8880 v3 processor operating at 2.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The server provides 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, alongside 45 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates 244.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory allocation of 30.5 GB per vCPU. Local storage includes a single 240 GB SSD, while baseline network bandwidth is rated at 1 Gbps. The instance contains no dedicated GPUs.

Benchmark results highlight an older CPU architecture with limited compute throughput. In synthetic CPU evaluations, the instance scored 740.09 on stress-ng single-core (bottom 10%) and 4139.38 on multi-core tests (bottom 25%). Geekbench testing yielded 841.0 in single-core and 3121.0 in multi-core metrics, reflecting lower per-core execution speeds. Memory bandwidth registered 36.34 GB/sec for uncached reads and 21.23 GB/sec for writes on 256 MB blocks. Database operations under PassMark measured 1981.96, and Redis SET throughput reached 4.87 million operations per second.

The primary tradeoff of the x1e.2xlarge is its specialized hardware profile, offering an extreme ratio of RAM relative to CPU capability. While raw processing and memory bandwidth are weak compared to newer generations, the 244.0 GB memory pool allows large datasets to reside entirely in memory. It is suited for in-memory databases, caching engines, and memory-bound enterprise applications that do not require high computational density.
